analysis.title: fvTrace
analysis.summary: What fvTrace itself can claim about its checker and engine: each claim rests on Lean proofs of the code fvTrace runs.

questions.title: Checking
questions.text: Does fvtrace check accept exactly the traces that fvTrace can evaluate?

questions.title: Verdicts
questions.text: When fvTrace gives a verdict, does it rest on what the trace records?

questions.title: Plans
questions.text: Are suggested plans the best that the suggested experiments allow?

questions.title: Isolation
questions.text: Can a what-if or another site reach claims it should not touch?

facts.subject: S
facts.text: The well-formedness check in fvtrace check reports no violation exactly when the decoded trace is well-formed.

evidence.verifier: Lean 4.35.0 kernel; replayed by lean4lean and nanoda (tools/trust.sh)

facts.subject: S
facts.text: Every violation that the well-formedness check in fvtrace check reports names a rule that the decoded trace breaks.

evidence.verifier: Lean 4.35.0 kernel; replayed by lean4lean and nanoda (tools/trust.sh)

facts.subject: S
facts.text: With no what-if, Can claim implies every need is recorded verified with a current receipt.

evidence.verifier: Lean 4.35.0 kernel; replayed by lean4lean and nanoda (tools/trust.sh)

facts.subject: S
facts.text: A claim whose entailment is human-ruled or empirical never reads Can claim.

evidence.verifier: Lean 4.35.0 kernel; replayed by lean4lean and nanoda (tools/trust.sh)

facts.subject: S
facts.text: Cannot claim holds exactly when a need is violated, the claim needs both sides of a verified or assumed exclusion, or both sides of such an exclusion hold on the claim's subject.

evidence.verifier: Lean 4.35.0 kernel; replayed by lean4lean and nanoda (tools/trust.sh)

facts.subject: S
facts.text: A planned set of experiments is prerequisite-closed, keeps the subject consistent and reports the state it reaches.

evidence.verifier: Lean 4.35.0 kernel; replayed by lean4lean and nanoda (tools/trust.sh)

facts.subject: S
facts.text: No prerequisite-closed, consistent set of experiments beats a plan's state, or matches it at strictly lower cost.

evidence.verifier: Lean 4.35.0 kernel; replayed by lean4lean and nanoda (tools/trust.sh)

facts.subject: S
facts.text: Two what-ifs that agree on a subject's facts give each claim on that subject the same state and breakdown.

evidence.verifier: Lean 4.35.0 kernel; replayed by lean4lean and nanoda (tools/trust.sh)

facts.subject: S
facts.text: The fvtrace binary runs the Lean definitions that the proofs are about.

facts.subject: S
facts.text: fvtrace hashes evidence files with the verified HACL* SHA-256, called unchanged.

evidence.summary: HACL* is verified in F*; tools/vendor-hacl.sh holds the vendored files byte-equal to the pinned release.

facts.subject: S
facts.text: fvtrace serve sends its page and claims only in answer to GET requests that name an allowed Host and carry the run's token.

evidence.summary: Tests/Server.lean checks each access decision of Server.decide.

facts.subject: S
facts.text: Without --cached, fvtrace reads every evidence file again and calls a receipt current only when each file has its pinned SHA-256 digest and the fact's wording is unchanged.

evidence.summary: Tests/Receipt.lean checks current, changed, missing and escaping evidence files and reworded facts against real files.

claims.question: Q1
claims.subject: S
claims.text: The well-formedness check in fvtrace check accepts a decoded trace exactly when it is well-formed, and each violation it reports is real.

claims.question: Q2
claims.subject: S
claims.text: With no what-if and without --cached, a claim reads Can claim only when every fact it needs is verified and its evidence is unchanged since it was pinned.

claims.question: Q2
claims.subject: S
claims.text: A claim whose entailment rests on a human ruling or on empirical evidence never reads Can claim.

claims.question: Q2
claims.subject: S
claims.text: Every Cannot claim has a stated reason: a violated fact, a verified or assumed exclusion between two of its needs, or a conflicting what-if on its subject.

claims.question: Q3
claims.subject: S
claims.text: A suggested plan includes its prerequisites, and no other consistent set of suggested experiments reaches a higher verdict or the same verdict at lower effort.

claims.question: Q4
claims.subject: S
claims.text: A what-if on the facts of one subject leaves the claims on other subjects unchanged.

claims.question: Q4
claims.subject: S
claims.text: A page from another site can never read the claims that fvtrace serve shows.

experiments.subject: S
experiments.title: Prove the server's access rules
experiments.method: State Server.decide's access rules in Fvtrace/Spec and prove them in Lean.
experiments.caveat: A proof covers Server.decide; the HTTP library that calls it stays trusted.
